chunks: Al-Shaykh, may Allah Most High support him, informed me from Abū al-Qāsim Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad, from Muḥammad ibn Yaʿqūb, from al-Ḥusayn ibn Muḥammad, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿĀmir, from ʿAlī ibn Mahziyār, from al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd, from Muḥammad ibn al-Fuḍayl, who said:

I asked Abā al-Ḥasan عليه السلام about a woman who embraces her husband from behind and moves upon his back, then desire comes to her and she emits fluid: is ghusl obligatory upon her, or is ghusl not obligatory upon her? He said: “When desire comes and she emits fluid, ghusl becomes obligatory upon her.”

key_terms.الشَّهْوَةُ: sexual desire that leads to the legal consequence mentioned
key_terms.الْغُسْلُ: the ritual bath that becomes obligatory
key_terms.الْمَاءَ: the emitted fluid referred to in the ruling
key_terms.الْمَرْأَةِ: the woman about whom the legal ruling is being asked
key_terms.زَوْجَهَا: her husband, in the spousal context of the ruling
key_terms.وَجَبَ: became obligatory; established as legally required

ai.seo_question: When does ghusl become obligatory for a woman if she experiences desire and emits fluid?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning janabah and ghusl for a woman. It states that when sexual desire occurs and fluid is emitted, ghusl becomes obligatory upon her, even in the circumstance described in the question.
